e-5484.knowledge_point: Calculating the Components of an Eigenvector Corresponding to an Eigenvalue
e-5484.problem:
If ![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/linear/14069178/assets/c3f5f7169fd10d5710a95d0eab9c290faa04a544ac646a2ebcd24aa6b7e5f714.png) is an eigenvector of ![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/linear/14069178/assets/69c5e6ae96062d7c8e289e1f0070ab3874b15d0b42bb9300a50b9315723cfd8f.png)
that corresponds to the eigenvalue $\,\lambda=1$, then what is the value of $\,\dfrac{b}{a}\,?$
e-5484.worked_solution:
To compute the eigenvectors of a matrix, we need to find non-zero solutions of the matrix equation 

$$
(A - \lambda I) \textbf{x}=\mathbf{0}.
$$

 

In our case, we have $\,\lambda =1.$ So, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}A-\lambda I & =[\begin{aligned}2 & 5 \\ -1 & -4\end{aligned}]-[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 \\ 0 & 1\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}1 & 5 \\ -1 & -5\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

We have to solve the corresponding homogeneous system of linear equations:

$$
{\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}+5{x}_{2}=0 \\ -{x}_{1}-5{x}_{2}=0\end{aligned}
$$

So, we row-reduce the augmented matrix $M$ to row echelon form using Gaussian elimination, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}M & =[\begin{aligned}1 & 5 & 0 \\ -1 & -5 & 0\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2}:={R}_{2}+{R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 5 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

In the reduced matrix above, there is one pivot column (the $1$st one). So, $x_2$ is a free variable. 

From the first equation, we obtain 

$$
x_1+5x_2=0
\qquad\Longrightarrow\qquad
x_1=-5x_2.
$$

Therefore, the general solution is

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/linear/14069178/assets/f8c4aba8e8fb922f08741deb8df0fe4f47c64c29b647fec7da2b0ce1b4367225.png)

Setting, for instance, $x_2=-1,$ we get the following eigenvector:

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/linear/14069178/assets/5f7d229b6636bbfbe8eab4bdb7a6b8e72bb21c9cc9e66b1b4d607fd0e5e352e0.png)

Finally, $\dfrac{b}{a}=\dfrac{-1}{5}=-\dfrac{1}{5}.$

e-5483.worked_solution:
To compute the eigenvectors of a matrix, we need to find non-zero solutions of the matrix equation 

$$
(A - \lambda I) \textbf{x}=\mathbf{0}.
$$

 

In our case, we have $\,\lambda =2.$ So, we get 

$$
\begin{aligned}A-\lambda I & =[\begin{aligned}7 & -4 \\ 5 & -2\end{aligned}]-2[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 \\ 0 & 1\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}5 & -4 \\ 5 & -4\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}

We have to solve the corresponding homogeneous system of linear equations:

$$
{\begin{aligned}5{x}_{1}-4{x}_{2}=0 \\ 5{x}_{1}-4{x}_{2}=0\end{aligned}
$$

So, we row-reduce the augmented matrix $M$ to row echelon form using Gaussian elimination, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}M & =[\begin{aligned}5 & -4 & 0 \\ 5 & -4 & 0\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2}:={R}_{2}+(-1){R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}5 & -4 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

In the reduced matrix above, there is one pivot column (the $1$st one). So, $x_2$ is a free variable. 

From the first equation, we obtain 

$$
5x_1-4x_2=0
\qquad\Longrightarrow\qquad
x_1=\dfrac{4}{5}x_2.
$$

Therefore, the general solution is

e-5485.problem:
Given that $\lambda=1$ and $\lambda=-4$ are the eigenvalues of the matrix
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/linear/14069178/assets/10510533350f1e77e4918cb4aff9edafe5ced005efc845becc8c1558bdd62811.png)
find two linearly independent eigenvectors of $A.$
e-5485.worked_solution:
We can get two linearly independent eigenvectors by simply finding eigenvectors corresponding to the different eigenvalues.

To compute the eigenvectors of a matrix, we need to find non-zero solutions of the matrix equation 

$$
(A - \lambda I) \textbf{x}=\mathbf{0}.
$$

With that in mind, let's consider each of the eigenvalues separately. 

- For $\lambda =1,$ we have

$$
\begin{aligned}A-\lambda I & =[\begin{aligned}1 & -1 \\ 0 & -4\end{aligned}]-1[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 \\ 0 & 1\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}0 & -1 \\ 0 & -5\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

We have to solve the corresponding system of linear equations:

$$
{\begin{aligned}-{x}_{2}=0 \\ -5{x}_{2}=0\end{aligned}
$$

So, we row-reduce the augmented matrix $M$ to row echelon form using Gaussian elimination, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}M & =[\begin{aligned}0 & -1 & 0 \\ 0 & -5 & 0\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2}:={R}_{2}+(-5){R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}0 & -1 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

In the reduced matrix above, there is one pivot column (the $2$nd one). So, $x_1$ is a free variable. 
From the first equation, we obtain  $x_2=0.$ Therefore, the general solution is
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/linear/14069178/assets/97e9cc73b2d39b924618c1372bf680ebf7d4374d1cf4fa9c3bc7e9afc05b06ea.png)
Setting, for instance, $x_1=1,$ we get the eigenvector 
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/linear/14069178/assets/a01037d3f9d9e090010a555fa0e14d6bce72da48c59bd74b0f7dad6afcee71ba.png)

- For $\lambda =-4,$ we have

$$
\begin{aligned}A-\lambda I & =[\begin{aligned}1 & -1 \\ 0 & -4\end{aligned}]-(-4)[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 \\ 0 & 1\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}5 & -1 \\ 0 & 0\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

We have to solve the corresponding system of linear equations:

$$
{\begin{aligned}5{x}_{1}-{x}_{2}=0 \\ 0=0\end{aligned}
$$

So, we row-reduce the augmented matrix $M$ to row echelon form using Gaussian elimination, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}M & =[\begin{aligned}5 & -1 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

In the matrix above, there is one pivot column (the $1$st one). So, $x_2$ is a free variable. 
From the first equation, we obtain $x_1=\dfrac{1}{5}x_2.$ Therefore, the general solution is
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/linear/14069178/assets/34313b24e58011d8be4790d57cd57d4800944903ff16dd20068b45bab2a7d261.png)
Setting, for instance, $x_2=5,$ we get the eigenvector

after.name: Question 1
after.problem:
If $v=[\begin{aligned}a \\ b\end{aligned}]$ is an eigenvector of 
$A=[\begin{aligned}-4 & 2 \\ 6 & 7\end{aligned}]$
that corresponds to the eigenvalue $\lambda =8,$
then what is the value of $\frac{b}{a}?$
after.worked_solution:
To compute the eigenvectors of a matrix, we need to find non-zero solutions of the matrix equation 

$$
(A-\lambda I)\text{x}=0.
$$

 

In our case, we have $\,\lambda =8.$ So, we get 

$$
\begin{aligned}A-\lambda I & =[\begin{aligned}-4 & 2 \\ 6 & 7\end{aligned}]-8[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 \\ 0 & 1\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}-12 & 2 \\ 6 & -1\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

So, we have a system of linear equations 

$$
{\begin{aligned}-12{x}_{1}+2{x}_{2}=0 \\ 6{x}_{1}-{x}_{2}=0\end{aligned}
$$

with the augmented matrix $M$ which we reduce to row echelon form using Gaussian elimination, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}M & =[\begin{aligned}-12 & 2 & 0 \\ 6 & -1 & 0\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2}:={R}_{2}+\frac{1}{2}{R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}-12 & 2 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

In the reduced matrix above, there is one pivot column (the $1$st one). Thus, ${x}_{2}$ is a free variable. 

From the first equation, we obtain 

$$
-12{x}_{1}+2{x}_{2}=0\,⟹\,{x}_{1}=\frac{1}{6}{x}_{2}.
$$

Hence, the general solution is

$$
[\begin{aligned}\frac{1}{6}{x}_{2} \\ {x}_{2}\end{aligned}],\,{x}_{2}\in R.
$$

Setting, for instance, ${x}_{2}=-12,$ we get the eigenvector 

$$
v=[\begin{aligned}a \\ b\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}-2 \\ -12\end{aligned}]
$$

Finally, $\frac{b}{a}=\frac{-12}{-2}=6.$

content.problem:
If $v=[\begin{aligned}a \\ b\end{aligned}]$ is an eigenvector of 
$A=[\begin{aligned}-4 & 2 \\ 6 & 7\end{aligned}]$
that corresponds to the eigenvalue $\lambda =8,$
then what is the value of $\frac{b}{a}?$
content.worked_solution:
To compute the eigenvectors of a matrix, we need to find non-zero solutions of the matrix equation 

$$
(A-\lambda I)\text{x}=0.
$$

 

In our case, we have $\,\lambda =8.$ So, we get 

$$
\begin{aligned}A-\lambda I & =[\begin{aligned}-4 & 2 \\ 6 & 7\end{aligned}]-8[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 \\ 0 & 1\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}-12 & 2 \\ 6 & -1\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

So, we have a system of linear equations 

$$
{\begin{aligned}-12{x}_{1}+2{x}_{2}=0 \\ 6{x}_{1}-{x}_{2}=0\end{aligned}
$$

with the augmented matrix $M$ which we reduce to row echelon form using Gaussian elimination, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}M & =[\begin{aligned}-12 & 2 & 0 \\ 6 & -1 & 0\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2}:={R}_{2}+\frac{1}{2}{R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}-12 & 2 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

In the reduced matrix above, there is one pivot column (the $1$st one). Thus, ${x}_{2}$ is a free variable. 

From the first equation, we obtain 

$$
-12{x}_{1}+2{x}_{2}=0\,⟹\,{x}_{1}=\frac{1}{6}{x}_{2}.
$$

Hence, the general solution is

$$
[\begin{aligned}\frac{1}{6}{x}_{2} \\ {x}_{2}\end{aligned}],\,{x}_{2}\in R.
$$

Setting, for instance, ${x}_{2}=-12,$ we get the eigenvector 

$$
v=[\begin{aligned}a \\ b\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}-2 \\ -12\end{aligned}]
$$

Finally, $\frac{b}{a}=\frac{-12}{-2}=6.$

after.name: Question 2
after.problem:
If $v=[\begin{aligned}a \\ b\end{aligned}]$ is an eigenvector of 
$A=[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 \\ 6 & -1\end{aligned}]$
that corresponds to the eigenvalue $\lambda =1,$
then what is the value of $\frac{b}{a}?$
after.worked_solution:
To compute the eigenvectors of a matrix, we need to find non-zero solutions of the matrix equation 

$$
(A-\lambda I)\text{x}=0.
$$

 

In our case, we have $\,\lambda =1.$ So, we get 

$$
\begin{aligned}A-\lambda I & =[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 \\ 6 & -1\end{aligned}]-1[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 \\ 0 & 1\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}0 & 0 \\ 6 & -2\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

So, we have a system of linear equations 

$$
{\begin{aligned}0=0 \\ 6{x}_{1}-2{x}_{2}=0\end{aligned}
$$

with the augmented matrix $M$ which we reduce to row echelon form using Gaussian elimination, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}M & =[\begin{aligned}0 & 0 & 0 \\ 6 & -2 & 0\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2}↔{R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}6 & -2 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

In the reduced matrix above, there is one pivot column (the $1$st one). Thus, ${x}_{2}$ is a free variable. 

From the first equation, we obtain 

$$
6{x}_{1}-2{x}_{2}=0\,⟹\,{x}_{1}=\frac{1}{3}{x}_{2}.
$$

Hence, the general solution is

$$
[\begin{aligned}\frac{1}{3}{x}_{2} \\ {x}_{2}\end{aligned}],\,{x}_{2}\in R.
$$

Setting, for instance, ${x}_{2}=3,$ we get the eigenvector 

$$
v=[\begin{aligned}a \\ b\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 3\end{aligned}]
$$

Finally, $\frac{b}{a}=\frac{3}{1}=3.$

If $v=[\begin{aligned}a \\ b\end{aligned}]$ is an eigenvector of 
$A=[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 \\ 6 & -1\end{aligned}]$
that corresponds to the eigenvalue $\lambda =1,$
then what is the value of $\frac{b}{a}?$
content.worked_solution:
To compute the eigenvectors of a matrix, we need to find non-zero solutions of the matrix equation 

$$
(A-\lambda I)\text{x}=0.
$$

 

In our case, we have $\,\lambda =1.$ So, we get 

$$
\begin{aligned}A-\lambda I & =[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 \\ 6 & -1\end{aligned}]-1[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 \\ 0 & 1\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}0 & 0 \\ 6 & -2\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

So, we have a system of linear equations 

$$
{\begin{aligned}0=0 \\ 6{x}_{1}-2{x}_{2}=0\end{aligned}
$$

with the augmented matrix $M$ which we reduce to row echelon form using Gaussian elimination, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}M & =[\begin{aligned}0 & 0 & 0 \\ 6 & -2 & 0\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2}↔{R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}6 & -2 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

In the reduced matrix above, there is one pivot column (the $1$st one). Thus, ${x}_{2}$ is a free variable. 

From the first equation, we obtain 

$$
6{x}_{1}-2{x}_{2}=0\,⟹\,{x}_{1}=\frac{1}{3}{x}_{2}.
$$

Hence, the general solution is

$$
[\begin{aligned}\frac{1}{3}{x}_{2} \\ {x}_{2}\end{aligned}],\,{x}_{2}\in R.
$$

Setting, for instance, ${x}_{2}=3,$ we get the eigenvector 

$$
v=[\begin{aligned}a \\ b\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 3\end{aligned}]
$$

Finally, $\frac{b}{a}=\frac{3}{1}=3.$

after.worked_solution:
To compute the eigenvectors of a matrix, we need to find non-zero solutions of the matrix equation 

$$
(A-\lambda I)\text{x}=0.
$$

 

In our case, we have $\,\lambda =-2.$ So, we get 

$$
\begin{aligned}A-\lambda I & =[\begin{aligned}2 & 3 \\ 20 & 13\end{aligned}]-(-2)[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 \\ 0 & 1\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}4 & 3 \\ 20 & 15\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

So, we have the homogeneous system of linear equations

$$
{\begin{aligned}4{x}_{1}+3{x}_{2}=0 \\ 20{x}_{1}+15{x}_{2}=0\end{aligned}
$$

with the augmented matrix $M$ which we reduce to row echelon form using Gaussian elimination, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}M & =[\begin{aligned}4 & 3 & 0 \\ 20 & 15 & 0\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}+(-5){R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}4 & 3 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

In the reduced matrix above, there is one pivot column (the $1$st one). Thus, ${x}_{2}$ is a free variable. 

From the first equation, we obtain 

$$
4{x}_{1}+3{x}_{2}=0\,⟹\,{x}_{1}=-\frac{3}{4}{x}_{2}.
$$

Hence, the general solution is

$$
[\begin{aligned}-\frac{3}{4}{x}_{2} \\ {x}_{2}\end{aligned}],\,{x}_{2}\in R.
$$

Setting, for instance, ${x}_{2}=4,$ we get the eigenvector 

$$
v=[\begin{aligned}a \\ b\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}-3 \\ 4\end{aligned}]
$$

Finally, $\frac{b}{a}=\frac{4}{-3}=-\frac{4}{3}.$

after.html:
Question 3
?

If v=[ab] is an eigenvector of A=[232013] that corresponds to the eigenvalue λ=−2, then what is the value of ba?

a
−3
b
4
c
−43
d
13
e
34
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

To compute the eigenvectors of a matrix, we need to find non-zero solutions of the matrix equation (A−λI)x=0.

In our case, we have λ=−2. So, we get

A−λI=[232013]−(−2)[1001]=[432015].

So, we have the homogeneous system of linear equations

{4x1+3x2=020x1+15x2=0

with the augmented matrix M which we reduce to row echelon form using Gaussian elimination, as follows:

M=[43020150]R2:=R2+(−5)R1∼[430000]

In the reduced matrix above, there is one pivot column (the 1st one). Thus, x2 is a free variable.

From the first equation, we obtain

4x1+3x2=0⟹x1=−34x2.

Hence, the general solution is

[−34x2x2],x2∈R.

Setting, for instance, x2=4, we get the eigenvector

v=[ab]=[−34]

Finally, ba=4−3=−43.

content.knowledge_point: Calculating the Components of an Eigenvector Corresponding to an Eigenvalue
content.problem:
If $v=[\begin{aligned}a \\ b\end{aligned}]$ is an eigenvector of 
$A=[\begin{aligned}2 & 3 \\ 20 & 13\end{aligned}]$
that corresponds to the eigenvalue $\lambda =-2,$
then what is the value of $\frac{b}{a}?$
content.worked_solution:
To compute the eigenvectors of a matrix, we need to find non-zero solutions of the matrix equation 

$$
(A-\lambda I)\text{x}=0.
$$

 

In our case, we have $\,\lambda =-2.$ So, we get 

$$
\begin{aligned}A-\lambda I & =[\begin{aligned}2 & 3 \\ 20 & 13\end{aligned}]-(-2)[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 \\ 0 & 1\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}4 & 3 \\ 20 & 15\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

So, we have the homogeneous system of linear equations

$$
{\begin{aligned}4{x}_{1}+3{x}_{2}=0 \\ 20{x}_{1}+15{x}_{2}=0\end{aligned}
$$

with the augmented matrix $M$ which we reduce to row echelon form using Gaussian elimination, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}M & =[\begin{aligned}4 & 3 & 0 \\ 20 & 15 & 0\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}+(-5){R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}4 & 3 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

In the reduced matrix above, there is one pivot column (the $1$st one). Thus, ${x}_{2}$ is a free variable. 

From the first equation, we obtain 

$$
4{x}_{1}+3{x}_{2}=0\,⟹\,{x}_{1}=-\frac{3}{4}{x}_{2}.
$$

Hence, the general solution is

$$
[\begin{aligned}-\frac{3}{4}{x}_{2} \\ {x}_{2}\end{aligned}],\,{x}_{2}\in R.
$$

Setting, for instance, ${x}_{2}=4,$ we get the eigenvector 

$$
v=[\begin{aligned}a \\ b\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}-3 \\ 4\end{aligned}]
$$

Finally, $\frac{b}{a}=\frac{4}{-3}=-\frac{4}{3}.$

If $v=[\begin{aligned}a \\ b\end{aligned}]$ is an eigenvector of 
$A=[\begin{aligned}4 & 1 \\ 3 & 2\end{aligned}]$
that corresponds to the eigenvalue $\lambda =1,$
then what is the value of $\frac{b}{a}?$

To compute the eigenvectors of a matrix, we need to find non-zero solutions of the matrix equation 

$$
(A-\lambda I)\text{x}=0.
$$

$$
\begin{aligned}A-\lambda I & =[\begin{aligned}4 & 1 \\ 3 & 2\end{aligned}]-1[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 \\ 0 & 1\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}3 & 1 \\ 3 & 1\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

So, we have the homogeneous system of linear equations

$$
{\begin{aligned}3{x}_{1}+{x}_{2}=0 \\ 3{x}_{1}+{x}_{2}=0\end{aligned}
$$

with the augmented matrix $M$ which we reduce to row echelon form using Gaussian elimination, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}M & =[\begin{aligned}3 & 1 & 0 \\ 3 & 1 & 0\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2}:={R}_{2}+(-1){R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}3 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

In the reduced matrix above, there is one pivot column (the $1$st one). Thus, ${x}_{2}$ is a free variable. 

From the first equation, we obtain 

$$
3{x}_{1}+{x}_{2}=0\,⟹\,{x}_{1}=-\frac{1}{3}{x}_{2}.
$$

Hence, the general solution is

$$
[\begin{aligned}-\frac{1}{3}{x}_{2} \\ {x}_{2}\end{aligned}],\,{x}_{2}\in R.
$$

Setting, for instance, ${x}_{2}=6,$ we get the eigenvector 

$$
v=[\begin{aligned}a \\ b\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}-2 \\ 6\end{aligned}]

after.name: Question 5
after.problem:
If $v=[\begin{aligned}a \\ b\end{aligned}]$ is an eigenvector of 
$A=[\begin{aligned}4 & 9 \\ 2 & 1\end{aligned}]$
that corresponds to the eigenvalue $\lambda =7,$
then what is the value of $\frac{b}{a}?$
after.worked_solution:
To compute the eigenvectors of a matrix, we need to find non-zero solutions of the matrix equation 

$$
(A-\lambda I)\text{x}=0.
$$

 

In our case, we have $\,\lambda =7.$ So, we get 

$$
\begin{aligned}A-\lambda I & =[\begin{aligned}4 & 9 \\ 2 & 1\end{aligned}]-7[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 \\ 0 & 1\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}-3 & 9 \\ 2 & -6\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

So, we have the homogeneous system of linear equations

$$
{\begin{aligned}-3{x}_{1}+9{x}_{2}=0 \\ 2{x}_{1}-6{x}_{2}=0\end{aligned}
$$

with the augmented matrix $M$ which we reduce to row echelon form using Gaussian elimination, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}M & =[\begin{aligned}-3 & 9 & 0 \\ 2 & -6 & 0\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}+(\frac{2}{3}){R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}-3 & 9 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

In the reduced matrix above, there is one pivot column (the $1$st one). Thus, ${x}_{2}$ is a free variable. 

From the first equation, we obtain 

$$
-3{x}_{1}+9{x}_{2}=0\,⟹\,{x}_{1}=3{x}_{2}.
$$

Hence, the general solution is

$$
[\begin{aligned}3{x}_{2} \\ {x}_{2}\end{aligned}],\,{x}_{2}\in R.
$$

Setting, for instance, ${x}_{2}=1,$ we get the eigenvector 

$$
v=[\begin{aligned}a \\ b\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}3 \\ 1\end{aligned}]
$$

Finally, $\frac{b}{a}=\frac{1}{3}.$

content.problem:
If $v=[\begin{aligned}a \\ b\end{aligned}]$ is an eigenvector of 
$A=[\begin{aligned}4 & 9 \\ 2 & 1\end{aligned}]$
that corresponds to the eigenvalue $\lambda =7,$
then what is the value of $\frac{b}{a}?$
content.worked_solution:
To compute the eigenvectors of a matrix, we need to find non-zero solutions of the matrix equation 

$$
(A-\lambda I)\text{x}=0.
$$

 

In our case, we have $\,\lambda =7.$ So, we get 

$$
\begin{aligned}A-\lambda I & =[\begin{aligned}4 & 9 \\ 2 & 1\end{aligned}]-7[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 \\ 0 & 1\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}-3 & 9 \\ 2 & -6\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

So, we have the homogeneous system of linear equations

$$
{\begin{aligned}-3{x}_{1}+9{x}_{2}=0 \\ 2{x}_{1}-6{x}_{2}=0\end{aligned}
$$

with the augmented matrix $M$ which we reduce to row echelon form using Gaussian elimination, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}M & =[\begin{aligned}-3 & 9 & 0 \\ 2 & -6 & 0\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}+(\frac{2}{3}){R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}-3 & 9 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

In the reduced matrix above, there is one pivot column (the $1$st one). Thus, ${x}_{2}$ is a free variable. 

From the first equation, we obtain 

$$
-3{x}_{1}+9{x}_{2}=0\,⟹\,{x}_{1}=3{x}_{2}.
$$

Hence, the general solution is

$$
[\begin{aligned}3{x}_{2} \\ {x}_{2}\end{aligned}],\,{x}_{2}\in R.
$$

Setting, for instance, ${x}_{2}=1,$ we get the eigenvector 

$$
v=[\begin{aligned}a \\ b\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}3 \\ 1\end{aligned}]
$$

Finally, $\frac{b}{a}=\frac{1}{3}.$

after.name: Question 6
after.problem:
Find an eigenvector of 
$A=[\begin{aligned}4 & -6 \\ -6 & 4\end{aligned}]$
that corresponds to the eigenvalue $\lambda =10.$
after.worked_solution:
To compute the eigenvectors of a matrix, we need to find non-zero solutions of the matrix equation 

$$
(A-\lambda I)\text{x}=0.
$$

 

In our case, we have $\,\lambda =10.$ So, we get 

$$
\begin{aligned}A-\lambda I & =[\begin{aligned}4 & -6 \\ -6 & 4\end{aligned}]-10[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 \\ 0 & 1\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}-6 & -6 \\ -6 & -6\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

So, we have the homogeneous system of linear equations

$$
{\begin{aligned}-6{x}_{1}-6{x}_{2}=0 \\ -6{x}_{1}-6{x}_{2}=0\end{aligned}
$$

with the augmented matrix $M$ which we reduce to row echelon form using Gaussian elimination, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}M & =[\begin{aligned}-6 & -6 & 0 \\ -6 & -6 & 0\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2}:={R}_{2}+(-1){R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}-6 & -6 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

In the reduced matrix above, there is one pivot column (the $1$st one). Thus, ${x}_{2}$ is a free variable. 

From the first equation, we obtain 

$$
-6{x}_{1}-6{x}_{2}=0\,⟹\,{x}_{1}=-{x}_{2}.
$$

Hence, the general solution is

$$
[\begin{aligned}-{x}_{2} \\ {x}_{2}\end{aligned}],\,{x}_{2}\in R.
$$

Finally, setting ${x}_{2}=1,$ we get the eigenvector 

$$
v=[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ 1\end{aligned}].
$$

after.name: Question 7
after.problem: Find an eigenvector of $A=[\begin{aligned}1 & 5 \\ 5 & 1\end{aligned}]$ that corresponds to the eigenvalue $\lambda =6.$
after.worked_solution:
To compute the eigenvectors of a matrix, we need to find non-zero solutions of the matrix equation 

$$
(A-\lambda I)\text{x}=0.
$$

 

In our case, we have $\,\lambda =6.$ So, we get 

$$
\begin{aligned}A-\lambda I & =[\begin{aligned}1 & 5 \\ 5 & 1\end{aligned}]-6[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 \\ 0 & 1\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}-5 & 5 \\ 5 & -5\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

So, we have the homogeneous system of linear equations

$$
{\begin{aligned}-5{x}_{1}+5{x}_{2}=0 \\ 5{x}_{1}-5{x}_{2}=0\end{aligned}
$$

with the augmented matrix $M$ which we reduce to row echelon form using Gaussian elimination, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}M & =[\begin{aligned}-5 & 5 \\ 5 & -5\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}+{R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}-5 & 5 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

In the reduced matrix above, there is one pivot column (the $1$st one). Thus, ${x}_{2}$ is a free variable. 

From the first equation, we obtain 

$$
-5{x}_{1}+5{x}_{2}=0\,⟹\,{x}_{1}={x}_{2}.
$$

Hence, the general solution is

$$
[\begin{aligned}{x}_{2} \\ {x}_{2}\end{aligned}],\,{x}_{2}\in R.
$$

Finally, setting ${x}_{2}=1,$ we get the eigenvector 

$$
v=[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 1\end{aligned}].
$$

Correct
EXPLANATION

To compute the eigenvectors of a matrix, we need to find non-zero solutions of the matrix equation (A−λI)x=0.

In our case, we have λ=6. So, we get

A−λI=[1551]−6[1001]=[−555−5].

So, we have the homogeneous system of linear equations

{−5x1+5x2=05x1−5x2=0

with the augmented matrix M which we reduce to row echelon form using Gaussian elimination, as follows:

M=[−555−5]R2:=R2+R1∼[−550000]

In the reduced matrix above, there is one pivot column (the 1st one). Thus, x2 is a free variable.

From the first equation, we obtain

−5x1+5x2=0⟹x1=x2.

Hence, the general solution is

[x2x2],x2∈R.

Finally, setting x2=1, we get the eigenvector

v=[11].

after.name: Question 8
after.problem: Find an eigenvector of $A=[\begin{aligned}22 & -40 \\ -5 & 5\end{aligned}]$ that corresponds to the eigenvalue $\lambda =-3.$
after.worked_solution:
To compute the eigenvectors of a matrix, we need to find non-zero solutions of the matrix equation 

$$
(A-\lambda I)\text{x}=0.
$$

 

In our case, we have $\,\lambda =-3.$ So, we get 

$$
\begin{aligned}A-\lambda I & =[\begin{aligned}22 & -40 \\ -5 & 5\end{aligned}]-(-3)[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 \\ 0 & 1\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}25 & -40 \\ -5 & 8\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

So, we have the homogeneous system of linear equations

$$
{\begin{aligned}25{x}_{1}-40{x}_{2}=0 \\ -5{x}_{1}+8{x}_{2}=0\end{aligned}
$$

with the augmented matrix $M$ which we reduce to row echelon form using Gaussian elimination, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}M & =[\begin{aligned}25 & -40 \\ -5 & 8\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}+\frac{1}{5}{R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}25 & -40 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

In the reduced matrix above, there is one pivot column (the $1$st one). Thus, ${x}_{2}$ is a free variable. 

From the first equation, we obtain 

$$
25{x}_{1}-40{x}_{2}=0\,⟹\,{x}_{1}=\frac{8}{5}{x}_{2}.
$$

Hence, the general solution is

$$
[\begin{aligned}\frac{8}{5}{x}_{2} \\ {x}_{2}\end{aligned}],\,{x}_{2}\in R.
$$

Finally, setting ${x}_{2}=5,$ we get the eigenvector 

$$
v=[\begin{aligned}8 \\ 5\end{aligned}].
$$

a
[8−5]
b
[85]
c

[140]

Incorrect
EXPLANATION

To compute the eigenvectors of a matrix, we need to find non-zero solutions of the matrix equation (A−λI)x=0.

In our case, we have λ=−3. So, we get

A−λI=[22−40−55]−(−3)[1001]=[25−40−58].

So, we have the homogeneous system of linear equations

{25x1−40x2=0−5x1+8x2=0

with the augmented matrix M which we reduce to row echelon form using Gaussian elimination, as follows:

M=[25−40−58]R2:=R2+15R1∼[25−400000]

In the reduced matrix above, there is one pivot column (the 1st one). Thus, x2 is a free variable.

From the first equation, we obtain

25x1−40x2=0⟹x1=85x2.

Hence, the general solution is

[85x2x2],x2∈R.

Finally, setting x2=5, we get the eigenvector

v=[85].

after.name: Question 9
after.problem: Find an eigenvector of $A=[\begin{aligned}17 & 3 \\ 4 & 6\end{aligned}]$ that corresponds to the eigenvalue $\lambda =5.$
after.worked_solution:
To compute the eigenvectors of a matrix, we need to find non-zero solutions of the matrix equation 

$$
(A-\lambda I)\text{x}=0.
$$

 

In our case, we have $\,\lambda =5.$ So, we get 

$$
\begin{aligned}A-\lambda I & =[\begin{aligned}17 & 3 \\ 4 & 6\end{aligned}]-5[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 \\ 0 & 1\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}12 & 3 \\ 4 & 1\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

So, we have the homogeneous system of linear equations

$$
{\begin{aligned}12{x}_{1}+3{x}_{2}=0 \\ 4{x}_{1}+{x}_{2}=0\end{aligned}
$$

with the augmented matrix $M$ which we reduce to row echelon form using Gaussian elimination, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}M & =[\begin{aligned}12 & 3 \\ 4 & 1\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}+(-\frac{1}{3}){R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}12 & 3 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

In the reduced matrix above, there is one pivot column (the $1$st one). Thus, ${x}_{2}$ is a free variable. 

From the first equation, we obtain 

$$
12{x}_{1}+3{x}_{2}=0\,⟹\,{x}_{1}=-\frac{1}{4}{x}_{2}.
$$

Hence, the general solution is

$$
[\begin{aligned}-\frac{1}{4}{x}_{2} \\ {x}_{2}\end{aligned}],\,{x}_{2}\in R.
$$

Finally, setting ${x}_{2}=4,$ we get the eigenvector 

$$
v=[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ 4\end{aligned}].
$$

before.name: Question 10
before.problem:
Find an eigenvector of

after.name: Question 10
after.problem:
Find an eigenvector of 
$A=[\begin{aligned}5 & -4 \\ -2 & -2\end{aligned}]$
that corresponds to the eigenvalue $\lambda =-3.$
after.worked_solution:
To compute the eigenvectors of a matrix, we need to find non-zero solutions of the matrix equation 

$$
(A-\lambda I)\text{x}=0.
$$

 

In our case, we have $\,\lambda =-3.$ So, we get 

$$
\begin{aligned}A-\lambda I & =[\begin{aligned}5 & -4 \\ -2 & -2\end{aligned}]-(-3)[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 \\ 0 & 1\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}8 & -4 \\ -2 & 1\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

So, we have the homogeneous system of linear equations

$$
{\begin{aligned}8{x}_{1}-4{x}_{2}=0 \\ -2{x}_{1}+{x}_{2}=0\end{aligned}
$$

with the augmented matrix $M$ which we reduce to row echelon form using Gaussian elimination, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}M & =[\begin{aligned}8 & -4 \\ -2 & 1\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}+(\frac{1}{4}){R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}8 & -4 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

In the reduced matrix above, there is one pivot column (the $1$st one). Thus, ${x}_{2}$ is a free variable. 

From the first equation, we obtain 

$$
8{x}_{1}-4{x}_{2}=0\,⟹\,{x}_{1}=\frac{1}{2}{x}_{2}.
$$

Hence, the general solution is

$$
[\begin{aligned}\frac{1}{2}{x}_{2} \\ {x}_{2}\end{aligned}],\,{x}_{2}\in R.
$$

Finally, setting ${x}_{2}=2,$ we get the eigenvector 

$$
v=[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 2\end{aligned}].
$$

a

[−12]
c

Correct

To compute the eigenvectors of a matrix, we need to find non-zero solutions of the matrix equation (A−λI)x=0.

In our case, we have λ=−3. So, we get

A−λI=[5−4−2−2]−(−3)[1001]=[8−4−21].

So, we have the homogeneous system of linear equations

{8x1−4x2=0−2x1+x2=0

with the augmented matrix M which we reduce to row echelon form using Gaussian elimination, as follows:

M=[8−4−21]R2:=R2+(14)R1∼[8−40000]

In the reduced matrix above, there is one pivot column (the 1st one). Thus, x2 is a free variable.

From the first equation, we obtain

8x1−4x2=0⟹x1=12x2.

Hence, the general solution is

[12x2x2],x2∈R.

Finally, setting x2=2, we get the eigenvector

v=[12].

Question 11
?

Given that λ=2 and λ=−1 are the eigenvalues of the matrix A=[4−25−3], find two linearly independent eigenvectors of A.

a
[11],[25]
b
[−21],[−15]
c
[1−1],[2−5]
d
[11],[23]
e
[31],[25]
Submit

decision.explanation: A(1,1)=(2,2)=2(1,1), and A(2,5)=(-2,-5)=-(2,5). Their determinant is 1·5−2·1=3≠0, so they are linearly independent.

after.name: Question 11
after.problem:
Given that $\lambda =2$ and $\lambda =-1$ are the eigenvalues of the matrix
$A=[\begin{aligned}4 & -2 \\ 5 & -3\end{aligned}]$,
find two linearly independent eigenvectors of $A.$
after.worked_solution:
To compute the eigenvectors of a matrix, we need to find non-zero solutions of the matrix equation 

$$
(A-\lambda I)\text{x}=0.
$$

With that in mind, let's consider each of the eigenvalues separately. 

- For $\lambda =2,$ we have

$$
\begin{aligned}A-\lambda I & =[\begin{aligned}4 & -2 \\ 5 & -3\end{aligned}]-2[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 \\ 0 & 1\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}2 & -2 \\ 5 & -5\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

So, we have a system of linear equations 

$$
{\begin{aligned}2{x}_{1}-2{x}_{2}=0 \\ 5{x}_{1}-5{x}_{2}=0\end{aligned}
$$

with the augmented matrix $M$ which we reduce to row echelon form using Gaussian elimination, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}M & =[\begin{aligned}2 & -2 & 0 \\ 5 & -5 & 0\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}+(-\frac{5}{2}){R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}2 & -2 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

In the reduced matrix above, there is one pivot column (the $1$st one). Thus, ${x}_{2}$ is a free variable. 
From the first equation, we obtain ${x}_{1}={x}_{2}.$ Hence, the general solution is

$$
[\begin{aligned}{x}_{2} \\ {x}_{2}\end{aligned}],\,{x}_{2}\in R.
$$

Setting, for instance, ${x}_{2}=1,$ we get the eigenvector 
${v}_{1}=[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 1\end{aligned}].$

- For $\lambda =-1,$ we have

$$
\begin{aligned}A-\lambda I & =[\begin{aligned}4 & -2 \\ 5 & -3\end{aligned}]-(-1)[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 \\ 0 & 1\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}5 & -2 \\ 5 & -2\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

So, we have a system of linear equations 

$$
{\begin{aligned}5{x}_{1}-2{x}_{2}=0 \\ 5{x}_{1}-2{x}_{2}=0\end{aligned}
$$

with the augmented matrix $M$ which we reduce to row echelon form using Gaussian elimination, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}M & =[\begin{aligned}5 & -2 & 0 \\ 5 & -2 & 0\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}+(-1){R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}5 & -2 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

In the reduced matrix above, there is one pivot column (the $1$st one). Thus, ${x}_{2}$ is a free variable. 
From the first equation, we obtain ${x}_{1}=\frac{2}{5}{x}_{2}.$ Hence, the general solution is

$$
[\begin{aligned}\frac{2}{5}{x}_{2} \\ {x}_{2}\end{aligned}],\,{x}_{2}\in R.
$$

Setting, for instance, ${x}_{2}=5,$ we get the eigenvector
${v}_{2}=[\begin{aligned}2 \\ 5\end{aligned}].$

Therefore, two linearly independent eigenvectors of the matrix $A$ are

$$
[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 1\end{aligned}],[\begin{aligned}2 \\ 5\end{aligned}].
$$

Question 11
?

Given that λ=2 and λ=−1 are the eigenvalues of the matrix A=[4−25−3], find two linearly independent eigenvectors of A.

a
[11],[25]
b
[−21],[−15]
c
[1−1],[2−5]
d
[11],[23]
e
[31],[25]
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

To compute the eigenvectors of a matrix, we need to find non-zero solutions of the matrix equation

(A−λI)x=0.

With that in mind, let's consider each of the eigenvalues separately.

  • For λ=2, we have A−λI=[4−25−3]−2[1001]=[2−25−5]. So, we have a system of linear equations {2x1−2x2=05x1−5x2=0 with the augmented matrix M which we reduce to row echelon form using Gaussian elimination, as follows: M=[2−205−50]R2:=R2+(−52)R1∼[2−20000] In the reduced matrix above, there is one pivot column (the 1st one). Thus, x2 is a free variable. From the first equation, we obtain x1=x2. Hence, the general solution is [x2x2],x2∈R. Setting, for instance, x2=1, we get the eigenvector v1=[11].

  • For λ=−1, we have A−λI=[4−25−3]−(−1)[1001]=[5−25−2]. So, we have a system of linear equations {5x1−2x2=05x1−2x2=0 with the augmented matrix M which we reduce to row echelon form using Gaussian elimination, as follows: M=[5−205−20]R2:=R2+(−1)R1∼[5−20000]. In the reduced matrix above, there is one pivot column (the 1st one). Thus, x2 is a free variable. From the first equation, we obtain x1=25x2. Hence, the general solution is [25x2x2],x2∈R. Setting, for instance, x2=5, we get the eigenvector v2=[25].

Therefore, two linearly independent eigenvectors of the matrix A are [11],[25].

content.knowledge_point: Finding Two Linearly Independent Eigenvectors of a 2x2 Matrix
content.problem:
Given that $\lambda =2$ and $\lambda =-1$ are the eigenvalues of the matrix
$A=[\begin{aligned}4 & -2 \\ 5 & -3\end{aligned}]$,
find two linearly independent eigenvectors of $A.$
content.worked_solution:
To compute the eigenvectors of a matrix, we need to find non-zero solutions of the matrix equation 

$$
(A-\lambda I)\text{x}=0.
$$

With that in mind, let's consider each of the eigenvalues separately. 

- For $\lambda =2,$ we have

$$
\begin{aligned}A-\lambda I & =[\begin{aligned}4 & -2 \\ 5 & -3\end{aligned}]-2[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 \\ 0 & 1\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}2 & -2 \\ 5 & -5\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

So, we have a system of linear equations 

$$
{\begin{aligned}2{x}_{1}-2{x}_{2}=0 \\ 5{x}_{1}-5{x}_{2}=0\end{aligned}
$$

with the augmented matrix $M$ which we reduce to row echelon form using Gaussian elimination, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}M & =[\begin{aligned}2 & -2 & 0 \\ 5 & -5 & 0\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}+(-\frac{5}{2}){R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}2 & -2 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

In the reduced matrix above, there is one pivot column (the $1$st one). Thus, ${x}_{2}$ is a free variable. 
From the first equation, we obtain ${x}_{1}={x}_{2}.$ Hence, the general solution is

$$
[\begin{aligned}{x}_{2} \\ {x}_{2}\end{aligned}],\,{x}_{2}\in R.
$$

Setting, for instance, ${x}_{2}=1,$ we get the eigenvector 
${v}_{1}=[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 1\end{aligned}].$

- For $\lambda =-1,$ we have

$$
\begin{aligned}A-\lambda I & =[\begin{aligned}4 & -2 \\ 5 & -3\end{aligned}]-(-1)[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 \\ 0 & 1\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}5 & -2 \\ 5 & -2\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

So, we have a system of linear equations 

$$
{\begin{aligned}5{x}_{1}-2{x}_{2}=0 \\ 5{x}_{1}-2{x}_{2}=0\end{aligned}
$$

with the augmented matrix $M$ which we reduce to row echelon form using Gaussian elimination, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}M & =[\begin{aligned}5 & -2 & 0 \\ 5 & -2 & 0\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}+(-1){R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}5 & -2 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

In the reduced matrix above, there is one pivot column (the $1$st one). Thus, ${x}_{2}$ is a free variable. 
From the first equation, we obtain ${x}_{1}=\frac{2}{5}{x}_{2}.$ Hence, the general solution is

$$
[\begin{aligned}\frac{2}{5}{x}_{2} \\ {x}_{2}\end{aligned}],\,{x}_{2}\in R.
$$

Setting, for instance, ${x}_{2}=5,$ we get the eigenvector
${v}_{2}=[\begin{aligned}2 \\ 5\end{aligned}].$

Therefore, two linearly independent eigenvectors of the matrix $A$ are

$$
[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 1\end{aligned}],[\begin{aligned}2 \\ 5\end{aligned}].
$$

Question 12
?

Given that λ=0 and λ=10 are the eigenvalues of the matrix A=[2−4−48], find two linearly independent eigenvectors of A.

a
[24],[1−2]
b
[31],[1−3]
c
[−2−2],[2−6]
d
[−4−2],[−24]
e
[−2−4],[−11]
Submit

decision.explanation: A(-4,-2)=(0,0), and A(-2,4)=(-20,40)=10(-2,4). Their determinant is (-4)(4)-(-2)(-2)=-20≠0, so these eigenvectors are linearly independent.

after.name: Question 12
after.problem:
Given that $\lambda =0$ and $\lambda =10$ are the eigenvalues of the matrix
$A=[\begin{aligned}2 & -4 \\ -4 & 8\end{aligned}]$,
find two linearly independent eigenvectors of $A.$
after.worked_solution:
To compute the eigenvectors of a matrix, we need to find non-zero solutions of the matrix equation 

$$
(A-\lambda I)\text{x}=0.
$$

With that in mind, let's consider each of the eigenvalues separately. 

- For $\lambda =0,$ we have

$$
\begin{aligned}A-\lambda I & =[\begin{aligned}2 & -4 \\ -4 & 8\end{aligned}]-0[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 \\ 0 & 1\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}2 & -4 \\ -4 & 8\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

So, we have a system of linear equations 

$$
{\begin{aligned}2{x}_{1}-4{x}_{2}=0 \\ -4{x}_{1}+8{x}_{2}=0\end{aligned}
$$

with the augmented matrix $M$ which we reduce to row echelon form using Gaussian elimination, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}M & =[\begin{aligned}2 & -4 & 0 \\ -4 & 8 & 0\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2}:={R}_{2}+2{R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}2 & -4 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

In the reduced matrix above, there is one pivot column (the $1$st one). Thus, ${x}_{2}$ is a free variable. 
From the first equation, we obtain  ${x}_{1}=2{x}_{2}.$ Hence, the general solution is

$$
[\begin{aligned}2{x}_{2} \\ {x}_{2}\end{aligned}],\,{x}_{2}\in R.
$$

Setting, for instance, ${x}_{2}=-2,$ we get the eigenvector 
${v}_{1}=[\begin{aligned}-4 \\ -2\end{aligned}].$

- For $\lambda =10,$ we have

$$
\begin{aligned}A-\lambda I & =[\begin{aligned}2 & -4 \\ -4 & 8\end{aligned}]-10[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 \\ 0 & 1\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}-8 & -4 \\ -4 & -2\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

So, we have a system of linear equations 

$$
{\begin{aligned}-8{x}_{1}-4{x}_{2}=0 \\ -4{x}_{1}-2{x}_{2}=0\end{aligned}
$$

with the augmented matrix $M$ which we reduce to row echelon form using Gaussian elimination, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}M & =[\begin{aligned}-8 & -4 & 0 \\ -4 & -2 & 0\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2}:={R}_{2}+(-\frac{1}{2}){R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}-8 & -4 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

In the reduced matrix above, there is one pivot column (the $1$st one). Thus, ${x}_{2}$ is a free variable. 
From the first equation, we obtain ${x}_{1}=-\frac{1}{2}{x}_{2}.$ Hence, the general solution is

$$
[\begin{aligned}-\frac{1}{2}{x}_{2} \\ {x}_{2}\end{aligned}],\,{x}_{2}\in R.
$$

Setting, for instance, ${x}_{2}=4,$ we get the eigenvector 
${v}_{2}=[\begin{aligned}-2 \\ 4\end{aligned}].$

Therefore, two linearly independent eigenvectors of the matrix $A$ are

$$
[\begin{aligned}-4 \\ -2\end{aligned}],[\begin{aligned}-2 \\ 4\end{aligned}].
$$

Question 12

Given that λ=0 and λ=10 are the eigenvalues of the matrix A=[2−4−48], find two linearly independent eigenvectors of A.

a
[24],[1−2]
b
[31],[1−3]
c
[−2−2],[2−6]
d
[−4−2],[−24]
e
[−2−4],[−11]
Submit
Incorrect
EXPLANATION

To compute the eigenvectors of a matrix, we need to find non-zero solutions of the matrix equation

(A−λI)x=0.

With that in mind, let's consider each of the eigenvalues separately.

  • For λ=0, we have A−λI=[2−4−48]−0[1001]=[2−4−48]. So, we have a system of linear equations {2x1−4x2=0−4x1+8x2=0 with the augmented matrix M which we reduce to row echelon form using Gaussian elimination, as follows: M=[2−40−480]R2:=R2+2R1∼[2−40000] In the reduced matrix above, there is one pivot column (the 1st one). Thus, x2 is a free variable. From the first equation, we obtain x1=2x2. Hence, the general solution is [2x2x2],x2∈R. Setting, for instance, x2=−2, we get the eigenvector v1=[−4−2].

  • For λ=10, we have A−λI=[2−4−48]−10[1001]=[−8−4−4−2]. So, we have a system of linear equations {−8x1−4x2=0−4x1−2x2=0 with the augmented matrix M which we reduce to row echelon form using Gaussian elimination, as follows: M=[−8−40−4−20]R2:=R2+(−12)R1∼[−8−40000]. In the reduced matrix above, there is one pivot column (the 1st one). Thus, x2 is a free variable. From the first equation, we obtain x1=−12x2. Hence, the general solution is [−12x2x2],x2∈R. Setting, for instance, x2=4, we get the eigenvector v2=[−24].

Therefore, two linearly independent eigenvectors of the matrix A are [−4−2],[−24].

verification.explanation: The worked solution confirms the earlier answer: A(-4,-2)=(0,0) and A(-2,4)=10(-2,4). The determinant of these vectors is -20≠0, proving linear independence.

content.knowledge_point: Finding Two Linearly Independent Eigenvectors of a 2x2 Matrix
content.problem:
Given that $\lambda =0$ and $\lambda =10$ are the eigenvalues of the matrix
$A=[\begin{aligned}2 & -4 \\ -4 & 8\end{aligned}]$,
find two linearly independent eigenvectors of $A.$
content.worked_solution:
To compute the eigenvectors of a matrix, we need to find non-zero solutions of the matrix equation 

$$
(A-\lambda I)\text{x}=0.
$$

With that in mind, let's consider each of the eigenvalues separately. 

- For $\lambda =0,$ we have

$$
\begin{aligned}A-\lambda I & =[\begin{aligned}2 & -4 \\ -4 & 8\end{aligned}]-0[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 \\ 0 & 1\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}2 & -4 \\ -4 & 8\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

So, we have a system of linear equations 

$$
{\begin{aligned}2{x}_{1}-4{x}_{2}=0 \\ -4{x}_{1}+8{x}_{2}=0\end{aligned}
$$

with the augmented matrix $M$ which we reduce to row echelon form using Gaussian elimination, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}M & =[\begin{aligned}2 & -4 & 0 \\ -4 & 8 & 0\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2}:={R}_{2}+2{R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}2 & -4 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

In the reduced matrix above, there is one pivot column (the $1$st one). Thus, ${x}_{2}$ is a free variable. 
From the first equation, we obtain  ${x}_{1}=2{x}_{2}.$ Hence, the general solution is

$$
[\begin{aligned}2{x}_{2} \\ {x}_{2}\end{aligned}],\,{x}_{2}\in R.
$$

Setting, for instance, ${x}_{2}=-2,$ we get the eigenvector 
${v}_{1}=[\begin{aligned}-4 \\ -2\end{aligned}].$

- For $\lambda =10,$ we have

$$
\begin{aligned}A-\lambda I & =[\begin{aligned}2 & -4 \\ -4 & 8\end{aligned}]-10[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 \\ 0 & 1\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}-8 & -4 \\ -4 & -2\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

So, we have a system of linear equations 

$$
{\begin{aligned}-8{x}_{1}-4{x}_{2}=0 \\ -4{x}_{1}-2{x}_{2}=0\end{aligned}
$$

with the augmented matrix $M$ which we reduce to row echelon form using Gaussian elimination, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}M & =[\begin{aligned}-8 & -4 & 0 \\ -4 & -2 & 0\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2}:={R}_{2}+(-\frac{1}{2}){R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}-8 & -4 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

In the reduced matrix above, there is one pivot column (the $1$st one). Thus, ${x}_{2}$ is a free variable. 
From the first equation, we obtain ${x}_{1}=-\frac{1}{2}{x}_{2}.$ Hence, the general solution is

$$
[\begin{aligned}-\frac{1}{2}{x}_{2} \\ {x}_{2}\end{aligned}],\,{x}_{2}\in R.
$$

Setting, for instance, ${x}_{2}=4,$ we get the eigenvector 
${v}_{2}=[\begin{aligned}-2 \\ 4\end{aligned}].$

Therefore, two linearly independent eigenvectors of the matrix $A$ are

$$
[\begin{aligned}-4 \\ -2\end{aligned}],[\begin{aligned}-2 \\ 4\end{aligned}].
$$

Question 13
?

Given that λ=−3 and λ=4 are the eigenvalues of the matrix A=[225−1], find two linearly independent eigenvectors of A.

a
[−1−3],[11]
b
[1−3],[2−2]
c
[−12],[−11]
d
[−25],[−3−3]
e
[25],[4−4]
Submit

decision.explanation: A(-2,5)=(6,-15)=-3(-2,5), and A(-3,-3)=(-12,-12)=4(-3,-3). Their determinant is 6+15=21≠0, so they are linearly independent.

after.name: Question 13
after.problem:
Given that $\lambda =-3$ and $\lambda =4$ are the eigenvalues of the matrix
$A=[\begin{aligned}2 & 2 \\ 5 & -1\end{aligned}]$,
find two linearly independent eigenvectors of $A.$
after.worked_solution:
To compute the eigenvectors of a matrix, we need to find non-zero solutions of the matrix equation 

$$
(A-\lambda I)\text{x}=0.
$$

With that in mind, let's consider each of the eigenvalues separately. 

- For $\lambda =-3,$ we have

$$
\begin{aligned}A-\lambda I & =[\begin{aligned}2 & 2 \\ 5 & -1\end{aligned}]-(-3)[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 \\ 0 & 1\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}5 & 2 \\ 5 & 2\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

So, we have a system of linear equations 

$$
{\begin{aligned}5{x}_{1}+2{x}_{2}=0 \\ 5{x}_{1}+2{x}_{2}=0\end{aligned}
$$

with the augmented matrix $M$ which we reduce to row echelon form using Gaussian elimination, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}M & =[\begin{aligned}5 & 2 & 0 \\ 5 & 2 & 0\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2}:={R}_{2}+(-1){R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}5 & 2 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

In the reduced matrix above, there is one pivot column (the $1$st one). Thus, ${x}_{2}$ is a free variable. 
From the first equation, we obtain  ${x}_{1}=-\frac{2}{5}{x}_{2}.$ Hence, the general solution is

$$
[\begin{aligned}-\frac{2}{5}{x}_{2} \\ {x}_{2}\end{aligned}],\,{x}_{2}\in R.
$$

Setting, for instance, ${x}_{2}=5,$ we get the eigenvector 
${v}_{1}=[\begin{aligned}-2 \\ 5\end{aligned}].$

- For $\lambda =4,$ we have

$$
\begin{aligned}A-\lambda I & =[\begin{aligned}2 & 2 \\ 5 & -1\end{aligned}]-4[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 \\ 0 & 1\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}-2 & 2 \\ 5 & -5\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

So, we have a system of linear equations 

$$
{\begin{aligned}-2{x}_{1}+2{x}_{2}=0 \\ 5{x}_{1}-5{x}_{2}=0\end{aligned}
$$

with the augmented matrix $M$ which we reduce to its row echelon form using Gaussian elimination, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}M & =[\begin{aligned}-2 & 2 & 0 \\ 5 & -5 & 0\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2}:={R}_{2}+\frac{5}{2}{R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}-2 & 2 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

In the reduced matrix above, there is one pivot column (the $1$st one). Thus, ${x}_{2}$ is a free variable. 
From the first equation, we obtain ${x}_{1}={x}_{2}.$ Hence, the general solution is

$$
[\begin{aligned}{x}_{2} \\ {x}_{2}\end{aligned}],\,{x}_{2}\in R.
$$

Setting, for instance, ${x}_{2}=-3,$ we get the eigenvector 
${v}_{2}=[\begin{aligned}-3 \\ -3\end{aligned}].$

Therefore, two linearly independent eigenvectors of the matrix $A$ are

$$
[\begin{aligned}-2 \\ 5\end{aligned}],[\begin{aligned}-3 \\ -3\end{aligned}].
$$

Question 13
?

Given that λ=−3 and λ=4 are the eigenvalues of the matrix A=[225−1], find two linearly independent eigenvectors of A.

a
[−1−3],[11]
b
[1−3],[2−2]
c
[−12],[−11]
d
[−25],[−3−3]
e
[25],[4−4]
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

To compute the eigenvectors of a matrix, we need to find non-zero solutions of the matrix equation

(A−λI)x=0.

With that in mind, let's consider each of the eigenvalues separately.

  • For λ=−3, we have A−λI=[225−1]−(−3)[1001]=[5252]. So, we have a system of linear equations {5x1+2x2=05x1+2x2=0 with the augmented matrix M which we reduce to row echelon form using Gaussian elimination, as follows: M=[520520]R2:=R2+(−1)R1∼[520000] In the reduced matrix above, there is one pivot column (the 1st one). Thus, x2 is a free variable. From the first equation, we obtain x1=−25x2. Hence, the general solution is [−25x2x2],x2∈R. Setting, for instance, x2=5, we get the eigenvector v1=[−25].

  • For λ=4, we have A−λI=[225−1]−4[1001]=[−225−5]. So, we have a system of linear equations {−2x1+2x2=05x1−5x2=0 with the augmented matrix M which we reduce to its row echelon form using Gaussian elimination, as follows: M=[−2205−50]R2:=R2+52R1∼[−220000] In the reduced matrix above, there is one pivot column (the 1st one). Thus, x2 is a free variable. From the first equation, we obtain x1=x2. Hence, the general solution is [x2x2],x2∈R. Setting, for instance, x2=−3, we get the eigenvector v2=[−3−3].

Therefore, two linearly independent eigenvectors of the matrix A are [−25],[−3−3].

content.knowledge_point: Finding Two Linearly Independent Eigenvectors of a 2x2 Matrix
content.problem:
Given that $\lambda =-3$ and $\lambda =4$ are the eigenvalues of the matrix
$A=[\begin{aligned}2 & 2 \\ 5 & -1\end{aligned}]$,
find two linearly independent eigenvectors of $A.$
content.worked_solution:
To compute the eigenvectors of a matrix, we need to find non-zero solutions of the matrix equation 

$$
(A-\lambda I)\text{x}=0.
$$

With that in mind, let's consider each of the eigenvalues separately. 

- For $\lambda =-3,$ we have

$$
\begin{aligned}A-\lambda I & =[\begin{aligned}2 & 2 \\ 5 & -1\end{aligned}]-(-3)[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 \\ 0 & 1\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}5 & 2 \\ 5 & 2\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

So, we have a system of linear equations 

$$
{\begin{aligned}5{x}_{1}+2{x}_{2}=0 \\ 5{x}_{1}+2{x}_{2}=0\end{aligned}
$$

with the augmented matrix $M$ which we reduce to row echelon form using Gaussian elimination, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}M & =[\begin{aligned}5 & 2 & 0 \\ 5 & 2 & 0\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2}:={R}_{2}+(-1){R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}5 & 2 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

In the reduced matrix above, there is one pivot column (the $1$st one). Thus, ${x}_{2}$ is a free variable. 
From the first equation, we obtain  ${x}_{1}=-\frac{2}{5}{x}_{2}.$ Hence, the general solution is

$$
[\begin{aligned}-\frac{2}{5}{x}_{2} \\ {x}_{2}\end{aligned}],\,{x}_{2}\in R.
$$

Setting, for instance, ${x}_{2}=5,$ we get the eigenvector 
${v}_{1}=[\begin{aligned}-2 \\ 5\end{aligned}].$

- For $\lambda =4,$ we have

$$
\begin{aligned}A-\lambda I & =[\begin{aligned}2 & 2 \\ 5 & -1\end{aligned}]-4[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 \\ 0 & 1\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}-2 & 2 \\ 5 & -5\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

So, we have a system of linear equations 

$$
{\begin{aligned}-2{x}_{1}+2{x}_{2}=0 \\ 5{x}_{1}-5{x}_{2}=0\end{aligned}
$$

with the augmented matrix $M$ which we reduce to its row echelon form using Gaussian elimination, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}M & =[\begin{aligned}-2 & 2 & 0 \\ 5 & -5 & 0\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2}:={R}_{2}+\frac{5}{2}{R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}-2 & 2 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

In the reduced matrix above, there is one pivot column (the $1$st one). Thus, ${x}_{2}$ is a free variable. 
From the first equation, we obtain ${x}_{1}={x}_{2}.$ Hence, the general solution is

$$
[\begin{aligned}{x}_{2} \\ {x}_{2}\end{aligned}],\,{x}_{2}\in R.
$$

Setting, for instance, ${x}_{2}=-3,$ we get the eigenvector 
${v}_{2}=[\begin{aligned}-3 \\ -3\end{aligned}].$

Therefore, two linearly independent eigenvectors of the matrix $A$ are

$$
[\begin{aligned}-2 \\ 5\end{aligned}],[\begin{aligned}-3 \\ -3\end{aligned}].
$$

after.name: Question 14
after.problem:
Given that $\lambda =7$ and $\lambda =29$ are the eigenvalues of the matrix
$A=[\begin{aligned}11 & -6 \\ -12 & 25\end{aligned}]$,
find two linearly independent eigenvectors of $A.$
after.worked_solution:
To compute the eigenvectors of a matrix, we need to find non-zero solutions of the matrix equation 

$$
(A-\lambda I)\text{x}=0.
$$

With that in mind, let's consider each of the eigenvalues separately. 

- For $\lambda =7,$ we have

$$
\begin{aligned}A-\lambda I & =[\begin{aligned}11 & -6 \\ -12 & 25\end{aligned}]-7[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 \\ 0 & 1\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}4 & -6 \\ -12 & 18\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

So, we have a system of linear equations 

$$
{\begin{aligned}4{x}_{1}-6{x}_{2}=0 \\ -12{x}_{1}+18{x}_{2}=0\end{aligned}
$$

with the augmented matrix $M$ which we reduce to row echelon form using Gaussian elimination, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}M & =[\begin{aligned}4 & -6 & 0 \\ -12 & 18 & 0\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}+3{R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}4 & -6 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

In the reduced matrix above, there is one pivot column (the $1$st one). Thus, ${x}_{2}$ is a free variable. 
From the first equation, we obtain  ${x}_{1}=\frac{3}{2}{x}_{2}.$ Hence, the general solution is

$$
[\begin{aligned}\frac{3}{2}{x}_{2} \\ {x}_{2}\end{aligned}],\,{x}_{2}\in R.
$$

Setting, for instance, ${x}_{2}=2,$ we get the eigenvector 
${v}_{1}=[\begin{aligned}3 \\ 2\end{aligned}].$

- For $\lambda =29,$ we have

$$
\begin{aligned}A-\lambda I & =[\begin{aligned}11 & -6 \\ -12 & 25\end{aligned}]-29[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 \\ 0 & 1\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}-18 & -6 \\ -12 & -4\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

So, we have a system of linear equations 

$$
{\begin{aligned}-18{x}_{1}-6{x}_{2}=0 \\ -12{x}_{1}-4{x}_{2}=0\end{aligned}
$$

with the augmented matrix $M$ which we reduce to row echelon form using Gaussian elimination, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}M & =[\begin{aligned}-18 & -6 & 0 \\ -12 & -4 & 0\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}+(-\frac{2}{3}){R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}-18 & -6 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

In the reduced matrix above, there is one pivot column (the $1$st one). Thus, ${x}_{2}$ is a free variable. 
From the first equation, we obtain ${x}_{1}=-\frac{1}{3}{x}_{2}.$ Hence, the general solution is

$$
[\begin{aligned}-\frac{1}{3}{x}_{2} \\ {x}_{2}\end{aligned}],\,{x}_{2}\in R.
$$

Setting, for instance, ${x}_{2}=3,$ we get the eigenvector 
${v}_{2}=[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ 3\end{aligned}].$

Therefore, two linearly independent eigenvectors of the matrix $A$ are

$$
[\begin{aligned}3 \\ 2\end{aligned}],[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ 3\end{aligned}].
$$

content.knowledge_point: Finding Two Linearly Independent Eigenvectors of a 2x2 Matrix
content.problem:
Given that $\lambda =7$ and $\lambda =29$ are the eigenvalues of the matrix
$A=[\begin{aligned}11 & -6 \\ -12 & 25\end{aligned}]$,
find two linearly independent eigenvectors of $A.$
content.worked_solution:
To compute the eigenvectors of a matrix, we need to find non-zero solutions of the matrix equation 

$$
(A-\lambda I)\text{x}=0.
$$

With that in mind, let's consider each of the eigenvalues separately. 

- For $\lambda =7,$ we have

$$
\begin{aligned}A-\lambda I & =[\begin{aligned}11 & -6 \\ -12 & 25\end{aligned}]-7[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 \\ 0 & 1\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}4 & -6 \\ -12 & 18\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

So, we have a system of linear equations 

$$
{\begin{aligned}4{x}_{1}-6{x}_{2}=0 \\ -12{x}_{1}+18{x}_{2}=0\end{aligned}
$$

with the augmented matrix $M$ which we reduce to row echelon form using Gaussian elimination, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}M & =[\begin{aligned}4 & -6 & 0 \\ -12 & 18 & 0\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}+3{R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}4 & -6 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

In the reduced matrix above, there is one pivot column (the $1$st one). Thus, ${x}_{2}$ is a free variable. 
From the first equation, we obtain  ${x}_{1}=\frac{3}{2}{x}_{2}.$ Hence, the general solution is

$$
[\begin{aligned}\frac{3}{2}{x}_{2} \\ {x}_{2}\end{aligned}],\,{x}_{2}\in R.
$$

Setting, for instance, ${x}_{2}=2,$ we get the eigenvector 
${v}_{1}=[\begin{aligned}3 \\ 2\end{aligned}].$

- For $\lambda =29,$ we have

$$
\begin{aligned}A-\lambda I & =[\begin{aligned}11 & -6 \\ -12 & 25\end{aligned}]-29[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 \\ 0 & 1\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}-18 & -6 \\ -12 & -4\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

So, we have a system of linear equations 

$$
{\begin{aligned}-18{x}_{1}-6{x}_{2}=0 \\ -12{x}_{1}-4{x}_{2}=0\end{aligned}
$$

with the augmented matrix $M$ which we reduce to row echelon form using Gaussian elimination, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}M & =[\begin{aligned}-18 & -6 & 0 \\ -12 & -4 & 0\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}+(-\frac{2}{3}){R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}-18 & -6 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

In the reduced matrix above, there is one pivot column (the $1$st one). Thus, ${x}_{2}$ is a free variable. 
From the first equation, we obtain ${x}_{1}=-\frac{1}{3}{x}_{2}.$ Hence, the general solution is

$$
[\begin{aligned}-\frac{1}{3}{x}_{2} \\ {x}_{2}\end{aligned}],\,{x}_{2}\in R.
$$

Setting, for instance, ${x}_{2}=3,$ we get the eigenvector 
${v}_{2}=[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ 3\end{aligned}].$

Therefore, two linearly independent eigenvectors of the matrix $A$ are

$$
[\begin{aligned}3 \\ 2\end{aligned}],[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ 3\end{aligned}].
$$

after.name: Question 15
after.problem:
Given that $\lambda =1$ and $\lambda =10$ are the eigenvalues of the matrix
$A=[\begin{aligned}4 & 6 \\ 3 & 7\end{aligned}]$,
find two linearly independent eigenvectors of $A.$
after.worked_solution:
To compute the eigenvectors of a matrix, we need to find non-zero solutions of the matrix equation 

$$
(A-\lambda I)\text{x}=0.
$$

With that in mind, let's consider each of the eigenvalues separately. 

- For $\lambda =1,$ we have

$$
\begin{aligned}A-\lambda I & =[\begin{aligned}4 & 6 \\ 3 & 7\end{aligned}]-1[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 \\ 0 & 1\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}3 & 6 \\ 3 & 6\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

So, we have a system of linear equations 

$$
{\begin{aligned}3{x}_{1}+6{x}_{2}=0 \\ 3{x}_{1}+6{x}_{2}=0\end{aligned}
$$

with the augmented matrix $M$ which we reduce to row echelon form using Gaussian elimination, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}M & =[\begin{aligned}3 & 6 & 0 \\ 3 & 6 & 0\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2}:={R}_{2}+(-1){R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}3 & 6 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

In the reduced matrix above, there is one pivot column (the $1$st one). Thus, ${x}_{2}$ is a free variable. 
From the first equation, we obtain  ${x}_{1}=-2{x}_{2}.$ Hence, the general solution is

$$
[\begin{aligned}-2{x}_{2} \\ {x}_{2}\end{aligned}],\,{x}_{2}\in R.
$$

Setting, for instance, ${x}_{2}=1,$ we get the eigenvector 
${v}_{1}=[\begin{aligned}-2 \\ 1\end{aligned}].$

- For $\lambda =10,$ we have

$$
\begin{aligned}A-\lambda I & =[\begin{aligned}4 & 6 \\ 3 & 7\end{aligned}]-10[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 \\ 0 & 1\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}-6 & 6 \\ 3 & -3\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

So, we have a system of linear equations 

$$
{\begin{aligned}-6{x}_{1}+6{x}_{2}=0 \\ 3{x}_{1}-3{x}_{2}=0\end{aligned}
$$

with the augmented matrix $M$ which we reduce to row echelon form using Gaussian elimination, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}M & =[\begin{aligned}-6 & 6 & 0 \\ 3 & -3 & 0\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2}:={R}_{2}+\frac{1}{2}{R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}-6 & 6 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

In the reduced matrix above, there is one pivot column (the $1$st one). Thus, ${x}_{2}$ is a free variable. 
From the first equation, we obtain ${x}_{1}={x}_{2}.$ Hence, the general solution is

$$
[\begin{aligned}{x}_{2} \\ {x}_{2}\end{aligned}],\,{x}_{2}\in R.
$$

Setting, for instance, ${x}_{2}=1,$ we get the eigenvector 
${v}_{2}=[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 1\end{aligned}].$

Therefore, two linearly independent eigenvectors of the matrix $A$ are

$$
[\begin{aligned}-2 \\ 1\end{aligned}],[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 1\end{aligned}].
$$

Given that λ=1 and λ=10 are the eigenvalues of the matrix A=[4637], find two linearly independent eigenvectors of A.

a
[−21],[11]
b
[−12],[11]
c
[−52],[31]
d
[21],[−11]
e
[2−1],[12]
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

To compute the eigenvectors of a matrix, we need to find non-zero solutions of the matrix equation

(A−λI)x=0.

With that in mind, let's consider each of the eigenvalues separately.

  • For λ=1, we have A−λI=[4637]−1[1001]=[3636]. So, we have a system of linear equations {3x1+6x2=03x1+6x2=0 with the augmented matrix M which we reduce to row echelon form using Gaussian elimination, as follows: M=[360360]R2:=R2+(−1)R1∼[360000] In the reduced matrix above, there is one pivot column (the 1st one). Thus, x2 is a free variable. From the first equation, we obtain x1=−2x2. Hence, the general solution is [−2x2x2],x2∈R. Setting, for instance, x2=1, we get the eigenvector v1=[−21].

  • For λ=10, we have A−λI=[4637]−10[1001]=[−663−3]. So, we have a system of linear equations {−6x1+6x2=03x1−3x2=0 with the augmented matrix M which we reduce to row echelon form using Gaussian elimination, as follows: M=[−6603−30]R2:=R2+12R1∼[−660000] In the reduced matrix above, there is one pivot column (the 1st one). Thus, x2 is a free variable. From the first equation, we obtain x1=x2. Hence, the general solution is [x2x2],x2∈R. Setting, for instance, x2=1, we get the eigenvector v2=[11].

Therefore, two linearly independent eigenvectors of the matrix A are [−21],[11].

content.knowledge_point: Finding Two Linearly Independent Eigenvectors of a 2x2 Matrix
content.problem:
Given that $\lambda =1$ and $\lambda =10$ are the eigenvalues of the matrix
$A=[\begin{aligned}4 & 6 \\ 3 & 7\end{aligned}]$,
find two linearly independent eigenvectors of $A.$
content.worked_solution:
To compute the eigenvectors of a matrix, we need to find non-zero solutions of the matrix equation 

$$
(A-\lambda I)\text{x}=0.
$$

With that in mind, let's consider each of the eigenvalues separately. 

- For $\lambda =1,$ we have

$$
\begin{aligned}A-\lambda I & =[\begin{aligned}4 & 6 \\ 3 & 7\end{aligned}]-1[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 \\ 0 & 1\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}3 & 6 \\ 3 & 6\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

So, we have a system of linear equations 

$$
{\begin{aligned}3{x}_{1}+6{x}_{2}=0 \\ 3{x}_{1}+6{x}_{2}=0\end{aligned}
$$

with the augmented matrix $M$ which we reduce to row echelon form using Gaussian elimination, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}M & =[\begin{aligned}3 & 6 & 0 \\ 3 & 6 & 0\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2}:={R}_{2}+(-1){R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}3 & 6 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

In the reduced matrix above, there is one pivot column (the $1$st one). Thus, ${x}_{2}$ is a free variable. 
From the first equation, we obtain  ${x}_{1}=-2{x}_{2}.$ Hence, the general solution is

$$
[\begin{aligned}-2{x}_{2} \\ {x}_{2}\end{aligned}],\,{x}_{2}\in R.
$$

Setting, for instance, ${x}_{2}=1,$ we get the eigenvector 
${v}_{1}=[\begin{aligned}-2 \\ 1\end{aligned}].$

- For $\lambda =10,$ we have

$$
\begin{aligned}A-\lambda I & =[\begin{aligned}4 & 6 \\ 3 & 7\end{aligned}]-10[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 \\ 0 & 1\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}-6 & 6 \\ 3 & -3\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

So, we have a system of linear equations 

$$
{\begin{aligned}-6{x}_{1}+6{x}_{2}=0 \\ 3{x}_{1}-3{x}_{2}=0\end{aligned}
$$

with the augmented matrix $M$ which we reduce to row echelon form using Gaussian elimination, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}M & =[\begin{aligned}-6 & 6 & 0 \\ 3 & -3 & 0\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2}:={R}_{2}+\frac{1}{2}{R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}-6 & 6 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

In the reduced matrix above, there is one pivot column (the $1$st one). Thus, ${x}_{2}$ is a free variable. 
From the first equation, we obtain ${x}_{1}={x}_{2}.$ Hence, the general solution is

$$
[\begin{aligned}{x}_{2} \\ {x}_{2}\end{aligned}],\,{x}_{2}\in R.
$$

Setting, for instance, ${x}_{2}=1,$ we get the eigenvector 
${v}_{2}=[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 1\end{aligned}].$

Therefore, two linearly independent eigenvectors of the matrix $A$ are

$$
[\begin{aligned}-2 \\ 1\end{aligned}],[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 1\end{aligned}].
$$
